description:
Could You Survive a Day on Io?

Episode 50 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌋
Io, Jupiter's volcanic moon: around 400 active volcanoes, lava fountains, plumes hundreds of kilometers high, and the tidal tug-of-war that keeps its insides molten. Episode 50!

➡️ Next stop: Titan
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

#space #io #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Could you survive one day on the most volcanic world in the solar system?
Io is one of Jupiter's moons, about the size of our Moon. But it looks like a pizza, and for good reason.
segments.headline: The pizza moon

segments.text: It has around four hundred active volcanoes. More than anywhere else in the solar system.
Some shoot plumes of gas hundreds of kilometers into space. Lava lakes glow on its surface.
segments.headline: Plumes into space

segments.text: Why so much fire on a small moon? Jupiter.
segments.headline: Blame Jupiter

segments.text: Io's orbit is slightly oval, so Jupiter's enormous gravity squeezes and stretches it, again and again.
segments.headline: Squeezed and stretched

segments.text: Its solid ground rises and falls by up to about one hundred meters, like a tide.
All that squeezing heats its insides, like bending a paper clip back and forth until it gets warm.
segments.headline: Heat from inside

segments.text: NASA's Juno spacecraft flew close to Io in twenty twenty-three and twenty twenty-four, capturing lava flows and mountains.
segments.headline: Juno up close

segments.text: Thank you for being here for fifty episodes. The journey continues.
Next stop: Titan. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
